description: For ages 6–9 with an adult: match every lid to its own pot and box in a kitchen shape puzzle.

body.heading: Mix them up
paragraphs: Your adult spreads out clean, empty containers and muddles all their lids into a separate pile. Round lids, square lids, big lids, tiny lids — all jumbled.
Every lid fits exactly one container. Your job is to find each lid's true partner.

body.heading: Match by shape and size
paragraphs: Start with the easiest matches. A huge lid can only fit a huge pot. A square lid needs a square box.
When a lid almost fits but wobbles, it is the wrong partner. The right lid clicks or settles on snugly.

body.heading: Beat the clock
paragraphs: Ask your adult to time you. Then muddle and play again, trying to beat your own time.
You used shape, size, and turning things over in your mind — that is real geometry, disguised as tidying up.

takeaway: Matching lids to containers is a shape-and-size puzzle, and the right lid always settles on snugly.
materials: Clean empty containers and their lids (an adult chooses)
safetyNotes: An adult chooses the containers — no glass, no sharp edges, and nothing that held cleaning chemicals. Wash everything before and after.
screenFreeExtension: Stack the containers inside each other like nesting dolls and see how small the pile can get.
